nodes.summary: For every positive integer $n$, the number of Stirling permutations $w$ of order $n$ that are extremely lucky, that is, whose set $\mathrm{Lucky}(w)$ of lucky cars has exactly $n$ elements, is the Catalan number $C_n$.
nodes.title: Extremely lucky Stirling permutations are counted by the Catalan numbers

nodes.summary: For every integer $n \ge 1$, the number of Stirling permutations $w$ of order $n$ that are extremely unlucky, that is, whose only lucky car is car $1$ ($\mathrm{Lucky}(w) = \{1\}$), is $(n - 1)!$.
nodes.title: Counting extremely unlucky Stirling permutations

nodes.summary: For every natural number $n$, the number of Stirling permutations $w$ of order $n$ in which exactly $n$ cars have nonzero displacement (equivalently, whose displacement composition $\mathrm{dis}(w)$ has exactly $n$ nonzero parts) is the Catalan number $C_n$.
nodes.title: Stirling permutations with $n$ nonzero displacements

nodes.summary: Let $w$ and $w'$ be Stirling permutations of order $n$, and suppose that $w$ is extremely lucky, that is, its set $\mathrm{Lucky}(w)$ of lucky cars has exactly $n$ elements. If every car has the same displacement in $w'$ as in $w$ (that is, $\mathrm{dis}(w') = \mathrm{dis}(w)$), then $w' = w$.
nodes.title: Extremely lucky Stirling permutations are determined by their displacements

nodes.summary: For every natural number $n$, there is a bijection between the Stirling permutations $w$ of order $n$ that are extremely lucky, that is, whose set $\mathrm{Lucky}(w)$ of lucky cars has exactly $n$ elements, and the Dyck words of semilength $n$ (valid parenthesizations of $n$ pairs of parentheses).
nodes.title: Extremely lucky Stirling permutations and Dyck words

nodes.summary: Let $w = w_1 \cdots w_{2n}$ be a Stirling permutation of order $n$ that is extremely lucky, that is, its set $\mathrm{Lucky}(w)$ of lucky cars has exactly $n$ elements, and let $1 \le i \le n$. If car $j$ is unlucky and exactly $i - 1$ of the cars $1, \dots, j - 1$ are unlucky, then car $j$ prefers spot $w_j = n - i + 1$ and has displacement $d(j) = 2i - 1$.
nodes.title: Unlucky cars of an extremely lucky Stirling permutation

nodes.summary: For every integer $n \ge 4$, the set $\{1, n - 1, 2n - 2\}$ is an $n$-admissible lucky set if and only if $n$ is even.
nodes.title: When $\{1, n - 1, 2n - 2\}$ is an admissible lucky set

nodes.summary: Let $n$, $h$ and $i$ be natural numbers with $h < i \le 2n$. The set $\{h, i\}$ is an $n$-admissible lucky set if and only if $h = 1$ and either $i > n$ and $i$ is odd, or $i \le n$.
nodes.title: Admissible lucky sets with two elements

nodes.summary: Let $n$ be a natural number. A finite set $S$ of natural numbers is an $n$-admissible lucky set if $S = \mathrm{Lucky}(w)$ for some Stirling permutation $w$ of order $n$, where $\mathrm{Lucky}(w)$ is the set of lucky cars of $w$.
nodes.title: Admissible lucky sets

nodes.summary: For every integer $n \ge 1$, the number of $n$-admissible lucky sets with exactly two elements is $n - 1 + \lceil (n - 1)/2 \rceil$.
nodes.title: Counting admissible lucky sets with two elements

nodes.summary: Let $n \ge 1$. If $S$ is an $n$-admissible lucky set, then $1 \in S$ and $2n \notin S$.
nodes.title: Necessary conditions for admissible lucky sets

nodes.summary: Let $n \ge 1$ and let $w$ be a Stirling permutation of order $n$, read as a parking function of length $2n$. The number of cars $i \in \{1, \dots, 2n\}$ with displacement $d(i) = 0$ is at least $1$ and at most $n$.
nodes.title: Number of cars with zero displacement

nodes.summary: The displacement composition of a word $w = w_1 \cdots w_{2n}$ is $\mathrm{dis}(w) = (d(1), \dots, d(2n))$, where $d(i)$ is the displacement of car $i$. For the Stirling permutations $1122$ of order $2$ and $11244233$ of order $4$, $\mathrm{dis}(1122) = (0, 1, 1, 2)$ and $\mathrm{dis}(11244233) = (0, 1, 1, 0, 1, 4, 4, 5)$ (the paper's Example 5.5).
nodes.title: Displacement compositions of 1122 and 11244233

nodes.summary: Let $w = w_1 \cdots w_{2n}$ be a word of natural numbers. Car $i$ prefers spot $q_i = ((w_i - 1) \bmod 2n) + 1$, where $w_i - 1$ is truncated at $0$; when every $w_i$ lies in $\{1, \dots, 2n\}$, this is $q_i = w_i$. Cars $1, \dots, 2n$ arrive in order, and car $i$ parks in the least spot $p(i) \in \{q_i, \dots, 2n\}$ not taken by an earlier car, or in $p(i) = q_i$ if there is no such spot. The displacement of car…
nodes.title: Displacement of a car

nodes.summary: Let $w$ be a Stirling permutation of order $n$, read as a parking function of length $2n$, with at least $3$ lucky cars, and let $x$ be the second-smallest lucky car of $w$. If $x \ge n$, then the number of lucky cars of $w$ is at most $w_1$, and every lucky car parks in one of the spots $1, \dots, w_1$.
nodes.title: The first preference bounds the lucky cars

nodes.summary: Let $n \ge 1$ and let $w$ be a Stirling permutation of order $n$, read as a parking function of length $2n$. Then (a) car $1$ is lucky; (b) the first car $i$ with $w_i = 1$ is lucky; (c) the number of lucky cars of $w$ is at least $1$ and at most $n$.
nodes.title: Basic properties of lucky cars

nodes.summary: Let $w$ be a Stirling permutation of order $n$, read as a parking function of length $2n$. Then $w$ has exactly $n$ lucky cars if and only if the second occurrences of the letters of $w$ appear in decreasing order: for all positions $a < b$ such that $w_a$ also occurs before position $a$ and $w_b$ also occurs before position $b$, we have $w_b < w_a$.
nodes.title: Characterization of extremely lucky Stirling permutations

nodes.summary: Let $n \ge 1$ and let $w$ be a Stirling permutation of order $n$, read as a parking function of length $2n$. Then car $1$ is the only lucky car of $w$ if and only if for every $x \in \{2, \dots, n\}$ and every position $i \le x$, we have $w_i < x$.
nodes.title: Characterization of extremely unlucky Stirling permutations

nodes.summary: Read as parking functions of length $4$, the Stirling permutation $1122$ has car $1$ as its only lucky car, and $1221$ has exactly cars $1$ and $2$ lucky: $\mathrm{Lucky}(1122) = \{1\}$ and $\mathrm{Lucky}(1221) = \{1, 2\}$.
nodes.title: Lucky sets of 1122 and 1221

nodes.summary: Let $w = w_1 \cdots w_{2n}$ be a word of natural numbers. Car $i$ prefers spot $q_i = ((w_i - 1) \bmod 2n) + 1$, where $w_i - 1$ is truncated at $0$; when every $w_i$ lies in $\{1, \dots, 2n\}$, this is $q_i = w_i$. Cars $1, \dots, 2n$ arrive in order, and car $i$ parks in the least spot $p(i) \in \{q_i, \dots, 2n\}$ not taken by an earlier car, or in $p(i) = q_i$ if there is no such spot. The lucky set…
nodes.title: The lucky set of a word

nodes.summary: Let $w = w_1 \cdots w_{2n}$ be a Stirling permutation of order $n$ and let $j \in \{1, \dots, 2n\}$. If $w_j < w_i$ for every $i < j$, then $j$ is odd.
nodes.title: Left-to-right minima of a Stirling permutation sit at odd positions

nodes.summary: Let $w = w_1 \cdots w_{2n}$ be a Stirling permutation of order $n$, read as a parking function of length $2n$, and let $x$ be a lucky car of $w$ such that exactly one lucky car of $w$ is smaller than $x$, so that $x$ is the second-smallest element of the lucky set $\mathrm{Lucky}(w)$. Then every car $c$ with $2 \le c \le x - 1$ parks in spot $w_1 + c - 1$.
nodes.title: Parking before the second lucky car

nodes.summary: Let $w = w_1 \cdots w_{2n}$ be a word of natural numbers. Car $i$ prefers spot $q_i = ((w_i - 1) \bmod 2n) + 1$, where $w_i - 1$ is truncated at $0$; when every $w_i$ lies in $\{1, \dots, 2n\}$, this is $q_i = w_i$. Cars $1, \dots, 2n$ arrive in order, and car $i$ parks in the least spot $p(i) \in \{q_i, \dots, 2n\}$ not taken by an earlier car, or in $p(i) = q_i$ if there is no such spot. The parking spot of car…
nodes.title: Parking spot of a car

nodes.summary: Let $n \ge 1$ and let $w = w_1 \cdots w_{2n}$ be a Stirling permutation of order $n$, read as a parking function of length $2n$. Then car $2n - 1$ is lucky, that is, belongs to the lucky set $\mathrm{Lucky}(w)$, if and only if $w_{2n-1} = 1$.
nodes.title: When the penultimate car is lucky

nodes.summary: Let $w = w_1 \cdots w_{2n}$ be a word of natural numbers, read as the preferences of $2n$ cars for spots numbered $0, \dots, 2n - 1$. Car $i \in \{1, \dots, 2n\}$ prefers the spot $(w_i - 1) \bmod 2n$, where $w_i - 1$ is truncated at $0$. When every $w_i$ lies in $\{1, \dots, 2n\}$, for example when $w$ is a Stirling permutation of order $n$, this is the spot $w_i - 1$, which is spot $w_i$ in the one-based numbering.
nodes.title: Zero-based preferences of a word

nodes.summary: Let $w = w_1 \cdots w_{2n}$ be a Stirling permutation of order $n$, read as a parking function of length $2n$, such that car $n$ is lucky and exactly one lucky car of $w$ is smaller than $n$, so that $n$ is the second-smallest element of the lucky set $\mathrm{Lucky}(w)$. (a) If $n$ is even, then $w_1 = 1$, $w_n = n$ and $\mathrm{Lucky}(w)$ has exactly $2$ elements. (b) If $n$ is odd and $w_1 = 1$, then $w_n = n$…
nodes.title: Stirling permutations whose second lucky car is $n$

nodes.summary: Let $w = w_1 \cdots w_{2n}$ be a Stirling permutation of order $n$, read as a parking function of length $2n$, and let $x$ be a lucky car of $w$ such that exactly one lucky car of $w$ is smaller than $x$, so that $x$ is the second-smallest element of the lucky set $\mathrm{Lucky}(w)$. If $x > n$, then $x$ is odd.
nodes.title: A second lucky car beyond $n$ is odd

nodes.summary: Let $w = w_1 \cdots w_{2n}$ be a Stirling permutation of order $n$, read as a parking function of length $2n$, and let $x$ be a lucky car of $w$ such that exactly one lucky car of $w$ is smaller than $x$, so that $x$ is the second-smallest element of the lucky set $\mathrm{Lucky}(w)$. If $w_1 = 1$, then $x \le w_x \le n$.
nodes.title: Preference of the second lucky car

nodes.summary: Let $w = w_1 \cdots w_{2n}$ be a Stirling permutation of order $n$ and let $\sigma$ be a permutation of $\{1, \dots, 2n\}$. Read words of length $2n$ as parking functions, and let $d(v)$ denote the total displacement of a word $v$, the sum of the displacements of its cars. Then the rearranged word $w \circ \sigma = w_{\sigma(1)} \cdots w_{\sigma(2n)}$ satisfies $d(w \circ \sigma) = d(w)$.
nodes.title: Total displacement of a Stirling permutation is invariant under rearrangement

nodes.summary: Let $w = w_1 \cdots w_{2n}$ be a Stirling permutation of order $n$, read as a parking function of length $2n$. Then the total displacement of $w$, the sum $d(1) + \dots + d(2n)$ of the displacements of its cars, is $n^2$.
nodes.title: Total displacement of a Stirling permutation

nodes.summary: Let $w = w_1 \cdots w_{2n}$ be a word of natural numbers, and for $i \in \{1, \dots, 2n\}$ let $d(i)$ be the displacement of car $i$ in $w$. The total displacement of $w$ is $d(w) = \sum_{i=1}^{2n} d(i)$.
nodes.title: Total displacement of a word

nodes.summary: Let $n \ge 1$. If $S$ is an $n$-admissible lucky set, then both $S$ and $S \cup \{2n + 1\}$ are $(n + 1)$-admissible lucky sets.
nodes.title: Extending admissible lucky sets

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
